fact: Water Valley's design guidelines want visible front landscaping to be primarily grass, finished within a year of the building permit on front yards and on any back yard next to or visible from open space, beaches or trails, and every landscaped area watered by an automatic sprinkler system on the Water Valley raw water tap.
quote: Visible front landscaping must be primarily grass and be completed within one year from building permit on front yards and on any back yard adjacent to or visible from open space, beaches, or trails. All landscape must be watered with an automatic sprinkler system and such system must be hooked up to the Water Valley raw water tap. All hose bibs must be hooked up to the Town of Windsor's potable system.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Architectural Standards Section 12, Landscaping (PDF p. 7; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024 of the watervalley.com PDF, file modified April 19, 2022)
notes: The original watervalley.com URL now redirects to thewatervalleycompany.com and returns 404; the Wayback copy was downloaded 2026-09-26 and read in full (45 pages; pages 27-40 are image-only and were read from the page images). No page uses the words artificial turf, synthetic turf or putting green. The master association's current guidelines are not posted publicly (its eunify portal refused connections on 2026-09-26).

fact: Water Valley's guidelines encourage grade-level decks, patios and outside living areas, discourage large elevated ones, and discourage landscape plans that draw a rigid property boundary between lots.
quote: Grade level decks, patios and outside living areas are encouraged and large elevated decks or patios are discouraged. … The intent of the approval process for landscaping is to encourage an open flowing relationship between lots. Any plan which defines a rigid property boundary is discouraged
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Architectural Standards Sections 11 (Site Grading) and 12 (Landscaping), PDF p. 7 (Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: Text layer is OCR of a scan; quote checked against the page image.

fact: Water Valley's guidelines require landscaping and other changes to a finished home to go to the Design Review Committee for approval before work starts, with a $50 submittal fee, $20 of it refunded on final approval.
quote: Additional construction to a home, landscaping or other improvements to a home after completion of an approved home must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for approval prior to initiation such changes and/or additions. A submittal fee of $50.00 must be included for any proposed changes, additional construction, landscaping or other improvements to the home. $20.00 of this fee is refundable upon final approval of the requested item(s).
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Section 3, Additional Construction and/or Exterior Changes after Completion of original Construction (PDF p. 3; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: The PDF's text layer is OCR and misreads some words (constrnction, Conunittee); the quote follows the page image.

fact: Water Valley's guidelines send ancillary improvements to existing homes, such as decks, exterior lighting, dog runs, fencing and play equipment, to the Design Review Committee before construction, and promise a written response within 60 working days of a complete submittal.
quote: All proposed ancillary improvements to existing homes in the Water Valley Subdivision must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for approval prior to commencement of construction. Such improvements include, but are not limited to: additions, decks, exterior lighting, dog runs, fencing, basketball hoops, play equipment … The Design Review Committee will review ancillary improvement plans and will provide a written response to the Owner within sixty (60) working days after complete submittal.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Section 7, Ancillary Improvements (PDF p. 4; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)

fact: Water Valley's landscaping checklist requires landscaping and fencing plans to be approved before any materials go in, and front yards to be 51% sod unless a xeriscape plan is approved as a special variance.
quote: Landscaping and fencing plans are required to be submitted and approved by the Water Valley Architectural Control Committee prior to installation of any materials. … Front yard to be 51% sod unless Xeriscape plan is submitted and approved for a special variance.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Landscaping Requirements and Landscape Check-list item 1 (PDF p. 24; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: The checklist names the Water Valley Architectural Control Committee; the rest of the booklet and the submittal form name the Design Review Committee.

fact: A Water Valley landscaping plan must label each area of ground cover by material, such as cedar mulch or 1-inch river rock, and show retaining walls, fencing, dog runs and decks with their distances from the lot lines.
quote: Designate areas of ground cover and label accordingly, cedar mulch, 1" river rock, decorative lava rock, etc. • Designate areas of rock trim or elevated retaining walls, their height and materials used. … • Designate the location, materials and height of any fencing or dog runs to be installed. • Designate location of new decks or structures to be constructed, including distances from lot lines.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Landscape Check-list item 4 (PDF p. 24; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)

fact: Water Valley's landscaping checklist gives two setbacks for play equipment: at least the equipment's tallest height and never under 5 feet from rear and side lot lines in item 1, and 8 feet from the property line in item 4.
quote: Playground equipment to be located from rear and side lot lines a minimum distance equal to the tallest height of the equipment, but not less than 5 ft. … Designate play equipment location (must be 8' from property line and non-obstructive to your neighbors).
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Landscape Check-list items 1 and 4 (PDF p. 24; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: The two items conflict (5 ft or the equipment's height vs 8 ft); the page says so and sends owners to the committee.

fact: Water Valley's landscaping checklist says researching and approving a landscaping, fencing or deck plan takes 48 to 72 hours, longer if information is missing.
quote: It takes 48 to 72 hours to research and approve your landscaping, fencing or deck plan. Longer if there is unidentified or missing information. Please do not submit a plan on a Thursday and expect to be planting on Friday evening.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Landscape Check-list item 6 (PDF p. 25; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: Conflicts with Section 7 (60 working days) and the ancillary form (up to 60 days); the page reports all three.

fact: Water Valley's guidelines say a new deck, porch, sun room, hot tub room or attached storage shed is approved by the Water Valley office first and then needs a building permit from the Town of Windsor.
quote: REMINDER: If you intend to build a new deck, porch, sun room, hot tub room or attached storage shed you must first submit the plan to the Water Valley Office for approval. Once approved, you will need to apply for a building permit from the Town of Windsor.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Landscape Check-list reminder (PDF p. 25; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)

fact: Water Valley's ancillary improvement form, edited September 16, 2021, lists front and rear landscaping, hardscape and play equipment among its request types, limits outbuildings to Pelican Hills and Hilltop Estates, asks for a plot-plan diagram with most requests, and gives the committee up to 60 days to respond.
quote: Front Landscaping … Rear Landscaping … Play Equipment (trampoline) … Concrete/Pavers (hardscape) … Outbuilding (Pelican Hills/Hilltop Estates Only) … A diagram, to include plot plan is required for most submissions. … I understand that HOA approval does not constitute approval of the local Town/County building departments and additional permitting may be required for my project. I understand that the Committee has up to 60 days to review and respond to my request.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association c/o Advance HOA Management, Ancillary Improvement Submittal Form, edited 9/16/21 (PDF p. 22 of the Design Guidelines; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)

fact: On Water Valley lots that back to open space, beaches or trails, side-lot privacy fencing stops 24 feet short of the back lot line, fencing within those 24 feet must be open design, and owners must complete and keep up visible back landscaping within a year of the home's completion.
quote: Open Space Lots - Side lot 6' privacy fencing on any lot which backs to open space, beaches, or trails shall not extend to within 24' of the back lot line. All fencing parallel with the back of the house and within 24' of the back of the lot must be Open Design and on the side or back lot lines. … All such lot owners must complete and maintain visible back landscaping within one year of home completion.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Section 14(c), Open Space Lots (PDF pp. 7-8; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: The scan defines Open Design as a two-rail fence with a handwritten note beside it: 'Three-rail - See EXIBIT A'. The page says 'open design' and does not count the rails.

fact: Water Valley's guidelines want play equipment near the house and away from open space and lot lines, without large canopies or structures that block neighbors' views of open space or lakes, and the Design Review Committee discourages landscaping that blocks those views.
quote: Playground equipment should be located near the house and away from open space and lot lines so as to not interfere with neighbors quiet yards. … shall not have large canopies or structures which would block neighbors views of open space or lakes. Views of Lakes and Open Spaces – Landscaping shall be full and attractive and the Design Review Committee will encourage the minimization of view blockage of lake and open spaces from your neighbors. Thus a large blue spruce on the back edge of the lot between your neighbors picture window and the lake would not normally be acceptable.
source_label: Water Valley Master Association, Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards, Section 18, Misc.: Playground Equipment; Views of Lakes and Open Spaces (PDF p. 9; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)

fact: The Hilltop Estates/Pelican Hills addendum requires a landscape plan by a landscape design professional, a sod front yard, no more than 20,000 square feet of irrigated sod per lot on a metered raw-water connection, at least four shade trees and two 6-foot conifers, and play equipment set back from rear and side lot lines by its height and never less than 5 feet.
quote: To be prepared by landscape design professional, showing locations and type of fencing, all planting bed locations, edging and mulch types, storage, lay areas, deck, etc. Shrubs, minimum 5 gallon. Lot trees, minimum of four (4) shade of minimum 1 ¾ in. caliber, with at least two (2) in the front yard and two (2) in the rear yard. Minimum two (2) 6' Coniferous per lot. Front yard to be sod. Consistent with approved Final Landscaping Plan. Maximum of 20,000 square foot of irrigated sod per lot. Irrigation system must connect to Water Valley Raw Water System and must be metered. Playground Equipment to be located from rear and side lot lines a minimum distance equal to the tallest height of the equipment, but not less than 5 ft.
source_label: Addendum to Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards for Hilltop Estates/Pelican Hills, page 1 of 2, Landscaping (PDF p. 10 of the Water Valley Design Guidelines; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: 'lay areas' is the document's own typo for play areas. The addendum covers Barn Owl Ct, Eagle Ct, Falcon Ct, Hawk Ct, Hilltop Circle/Drive, Horned Owl Ct, Kestrel Ct, Merlin Ln and Osprey Ct.

fact: The Hilltop Estates/Pelican Hills addendum lists the landscape plan, playhouses, play equipment, swing sets and site lighting among items needing approval, allows an outbuilding that matches the house with approval, and wants landscaping finished within 12 months of the certificate of occupancy.
quote: Out Building: Must be the same architecture, color and material quantity as house, must be submitted with site plan to be approved by A.C.C. … Completed landscaping within 12 months of certificate of occupancy. … Items That Need Approval: Storm Doors, Basketball Hoops, Playhouse, Dog Runs & Enclosures, Playground Equipment, Swing Sets, Sign, House Numbers, Cloths Lines, Site Lighting, Window Air Conditioners, Swamp Coolers, Firewood Storage, Change in Color Scheme, RV, Boat and Additional Vehicle Parking, Storage Sheds, Landscape Plan and other items at the sole discretion of the A.C.C.
source_label: Addendum to Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards for Hilltop Estates/Pelican Hills, page 2 of 2 (PDF p. 11 of the Water Valley Design Guidelines; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)

fact: Windsor's parcel map shows 97 parcels inside the three Hilltop Estates plats, which cover about 283 acres; the median parcel is about 105,800 square feet (about 2.4 acres), and 93 of the parcels are 2 acres or more.
quote: SUBMJRNAME: HILLTOP ESTATES · SUBNAME: HILLTOP ESTATES; HILLTOP ESTATES 2ND FG; HILLTOP ESTATES 3RD FG · MUNICIPALITY: WINDSOR · COUNTY: WELD
source_label: Town of Windsor GIS, Community/Parcels layer, parcels whose centroid falls inside the three Hilltop Estates plats of the Planning/Subdivisions layer (97 parcels; 283 plat acres; median about 105,800 sq ft, about 2.4 acres; 93 of 2 acres or more)
notes: Queried 2026-09-26: Planning/Subdivisions/MapServer/0 where SUBMJRNAME='HILLTOP ESTATES' (3 plats, 269.1 + 4.6 + 9.6 = 283.3 acres from Shape.STArea, EPSG 2231 US feet); Community/Parcels/MapServer/0 intersecting the plats' envelope (407 parcels), kept the 97 whose polygon centroid falls inside a plat. Parcel areas from Shape.STArea(): median 105,758 sq ft, quartiles 100,784 and 117,769, 93 at or above 87,120 sq ft. Street names on the parcels (Hilltop Cir/Dr, Kestrel, Barn Owl, Osprey, Merlin, Falcon, Horned Owl, Eagle, Hawk) match the addendum's street list.

fact: The Harbors addendum allows an optional boat house built in the house's materials, calls for black wrought-iron fencing along the rear, and requires front and back landscaping installed by a professional landscaping company within 8 months of occupancy, backed by a $10,000 deposit.
quote: Fence: Black Wrought Iron along rear with architectural pillars to match house. Boat House (Optional): Same architectural materials as house. Landscape: Must complete front and back within 8 months of occupancy and installed by professional landscaping company. $10,000 deposit retuned upon satisfactory completion.
source_label: Addendum to Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards for The Harbors (PDF p. 12 of the Water Valley Design Guidelines; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: 'retuned' is the document's own typo for returned.

fact: The Marina Doce addendum, effective September 18, 2006, accepts a xeriscape front yard only when the design includes a water feature, otherwise wants most of the front yard in sod, holds a $20,000 landscaping deposit from closing, and wants landscaping finished within 12 months of construction completion.
quote: Xeriscape plans acceptable if water feature is incorporated in front yard design. Otherwise, majority of front yard to be sod. $20,000 deposit required at closing to be returned after landscaping is installed to meet requirements. Landscaping to be completed within 12 months of construction completion.
source_label: Addendum to Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards for Marina Doce at Water Valley, effective September 18, 2006, Landscape (PDF pp. 19-20 of the Water Valley Design Guidelines; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: The addendum's landscape row opens 'To be designed and installed by a professional landscape com-' and the line breaks off in the document itself; the page says professional design and installation without quoting the broken line.

fact: The Water Valley South addendum, effective November 17, 2004, has professional landscaping companies install landscaping unless the DRC approves otherwise, requires DRC approval of any irrigation system's design before installation by DRC-approved irrigation companies, and lets only authorized personnel connect or disconnect a system from the raw water line, for a fee of no more than $1,000 unless the DRC approves otherwise.
quote: Unless otherwise approved by the DRC, all landscaping within Water Valley South shall be installed by professional landscaping companies which are either bonded or insured and must adhere to published Water Valley landscaping design requirements. … The Poudre Tech Metropolitan District (the "Metro District") owns and maintains a raw water irrigation system which provides a ¾" tap at the back of each Lot. … The design, materials, specifications and location of any irrigation system in Water Valley South must be approved by the DRC prior to construction or installation. … The design and installation of all irrigation systems within Water Valley South must be conducted by professional irrigation companies approved in advance by the DRC. … which fee shall not exceed One Thousand Dollars ($1,000.00) unless otherwise approved by the DRC.
source_label: Addendum to Design Guidelines & Architectural Standards for Water Valley South, effective November 17, 2004, Sections 9 and 10 (PDF pp. 13 and 16 of the Water Valley Design Guidelines; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)

fact: The 2014 design guidelines for Water Valley South's 15th and 16th subdivisions want 51% of the yard covered with grass or xeriscaping with a living appearance, and rear yards designed with grass, trees and shrubs.
quote: 51% of the yard must be covered with grass or zeroscaping done in a manner that it has a living, natural and attractive appearance. … Rear yards must also have an attractive design which includes grass, trees, and shrubs that are appropriate to the size and create a natural and living appearance.
source_label: Water Valley South 15th Subdivision Design Guidelines (4/28/2014) and 16th Subdivision Design Guidelines (6/18/2014), Required Landscaping (PDF pp. 34 and 39 of the Water Valley Design Guidelines; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)
notes: These pages have no text layer; read from the page images. 'zeroscaping' is the document's spelling. The 15th covers Beluga Dr, Cataluna Dr, Halibut Dr and Ibiza Ct; the 16th covers Longfin Ct/Dr and Stonefish Dr.

fact: The 2014 design guidelines for Water Valley South's 18th subdivision want at least 51% of the front yard and rear yard covered in live landscape material at maturity, allow xeric designs that meet the minimums, and require every landscape area on an automatic system connected to the Water Valley raw water tap.
quote: 9. A minimum of 51% of the front yard and rear yard shall be covered in live landscape material at maturity. 10. Xeric landscape designs are permissible provided minimum overages are met. … 19. All landscape areas shall be irrigated with a 100%, underground supplied automatic irrigation system connected to the Water Valley raw water tap.
source_label: 18th Subdivision Design Guidelines, Water Valley South (Baja, Los Cabos Dr, Marina Dr, Seahorse Dr, Shadow Lake Ct), 7/18/2014, Landscape Requirements (PDF p. 44 of the Water Valley Design Guidelines; Wayback Machine copy captured June 27, 2024)

fact: Ravina's guidelines under Water Valley Metropolitan District No. 3 prohibit artificial turf in front yards, require Architectural Review Committee approval for any other use except as law or ordinance provides otherwise, and keep synthetic turf off walks, front steps and decks.
quote: The total yard will consist of irrigated sod, non-irrigated material such as rock mulch, bark or other non-irrigable materials approved by the ARC except as otherwise provided by law or ordinance. Artificial turf is prohibited in front yards. All other uses must be approved by the ARC except as otherwise provided by law or ordinance. … 2.21. Entrances (Front) - Synthetic turf/sod is not allowed on walks, front steps or decks.
source_label: Ravina Subdivision and Water Valley Metropolitan District No. 3, Residential Improvement Guidelines and Site Restrictions (updated January 1, 2025), Sec. 2.10.4 Landscaping and Sec. 2.21 Entrances (Front)
notes: Downloaded 2026-09-26 from the district's ARC page and read in full with pdftotext. The document says it was prepared by Ravina Investments, LLC for the district and that the Declaration for Ravina Subdivision and Water Valley Metropolitan District No. 3 controls on any conflict.

fact: Ravina's guidelines want a landscaping plan showing fences, decks, sod, rock, the sprinkler plan and a drainage and grading plan that matches the municipality's, landscaping finished within 365 days of closing on the Poudre Tech non-potable system, and they let the committee ask for a drainage engineer's report at the owner's expense.
quote: Plans must depict proposed fences and gates, decks, sod, seeded areas, retaining walls (generally not permitted pursuant to Section 2.18), rock, railroad ties, sprinkler system plan, sizes and species of nursery material, and include a drainage and grading plan showing compliance with the municipality approved drainage and grading plan. … Landscaping must be completed within three hundred sixty five (365) days following closing. • Must be connected to the seasonal Non-Potable Water System that is operated by Poudre Tech Metropolitan District and subject to their Water Rules and Regulations. … The ARC may require a report from a drainage engineer at Owner's sole expense as part of the landscaping or improvement plan approval.
source_label: Ravina Subdivision and Water Valley Metropolitan District No. 3, Residential Improvement Guidelines and Site Restrictions (updated January 1, 2025), Sec. 2.10.4 Landscaping and Sec. 2.18 Drainage

fact: Ravina's guidelines set a one-time $50 review fee, send owners to the district if 30 days pass without a decision, and treat a second submittal left unanswered for 30 days as approved, but only for work fully described in the plans and in full compliance with the declaration and guidelines.
quote: A one-time review fee of $50 shall be paid to the District upon submission. … Failure of the ARC or designated representative to approve or disapprove plans and specifications within thirty (30) days of submittal requires contacting the District to obtain the status of the submittal. Occasionally a 2nd submittal will be required. If ARC fails to respond within thirty (30) days after the 2nd submittal, such 2nd submittal shall be interpreted as approval subject to compliance with the Declaration and subject to Section 1.8 of the Guidelines. Deemed approval shall only apply when matters specifically and sufficiently described in plans and specifications are submitted to, and received by, the ARC and are in full compliance with the Declaration and RIGSR.
source_label: Ravina Subdivision and Water Valley Metropolitan District No. 3, Residential Improvement Guidelines and Site Restrictions (updated January 1, 2025), Sec. 2.10.2 Submittal Fee and Sec. 2.10.5 Review and ARC Action

fact: Water Valley Metropolitan District No. 3 takes Ravina's architectural requests through its residential portal and says every property improvement or addition needs ARC review and approval, with a 30-day review period.
quote: ARC Requests can be submitted through the Residential Portal page. … *All property improvements/additions require ARC review and approval.  There is a 30-day review period*
source_label: Water Valley Metropolitan District No. 3, ARC Submittal, Review and Enforcement page

fact: Ravina's guidelines require ARC approval for play and sports equipment and generally hold playhouses and swing sets under 8 feet at the peak and 120 square feet inside, matched to the house and screened by landscaping and an approved fence.
quote: 2.39. Playhouses/Play Equipment/Sports Equipment - ARC approval required. General guidelines for play houses or swing set to be less than eight feet (8') in height at the peak and less than 120 square feet of interior floor space. Basic design, materials and colors must match the residence, and must be incorporated into, and at least screened by the landscape features and ARC approved fence.
source_label: Ravina Subdivision and Water Valley Metropolitan District No. 3, Residential Improvement Guidelines and Site Restrictions (updated January 1, 2025), Sec. 2.39

fact: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District charges for Water Valley's non-potable irrigation water with an annual capital fee of $277.68 per unit, billed at the start of the irrigation season, plus $4.53 per 1,000 gallons used.
quote: The water rate structure includes an Annual Capital Fee plus a water service fee charged at a rate of per $4.53 per 1,000 gallons of water used. The Annual Capital Fee is $277.68 per unit and is billed at the beginning of the irrigation season.
source_label: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District and Water Valley Metropolitan District Nos. 1 & 2, Non-Potable Irrigation Water page (2026 rates; the district's 2026 Schedule of Fees and Charges, effective April 1, 2026, lists $277.68 per single-family residential unit plus $4.53 per 1,000 gallons)
notes: The 2026 Schedule of Fees and Charges PDF linked from the page (effective April 1, 2026) shows the 2025 rate of $267.00 + $4.27/1,000 gallons rising to $277.68 + $4.53. The RainDance and Poudre Tech fact sheets share one district office.

fact: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District wants each non-potable meter pit and curb stop left exposed and clear of landscaping, rock, mulch, decks and patios, and says damage to either may be billed to the owner.
quote: All activations and deactivations of water service through a curb stop should be performed by District personnel only. The non-potable irrigation water meter pit and curb stop should be exposed and uninhibited by landscaping, rock, mulch, bird baths, decks or patios, etc. Costs associated with damage to the meter pit or curb stop may be billed back to the property owner.
source_label: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District and Water Valley Metropolitan District Nos. 1 & 2, Non-Potable Irrigation Water page, Water Meter And Curb Stop

fact: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District usually turns Water Valley's non-potable irrigation water on in mid-April and off in mid-October, and owners winterize their own irrigation systems.
quote: The Metro District typically activates the non-potable irrigation water supply in mid-April and turns it off in mid-October, weather permitting. … At the end of the irrigation season, owners are responsible for winterizing their own irrigation systems.
source_label: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District and Water Valley Metropolitan District Nos. 1 & 2, Non-Potable Irrigation Water page, Activation and Winterization

fact: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District's 2026 owner guide says each home's non-potable meter pit is in its back yard, with the hand valve and the blow-out port inside it.
quote: Meter pit is located in the back yard of each home. … The blow-out port is located within the meter pit. This is where owners should blow out their system at the end of the irrigation season.
source_label: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District, Non-Potable Irrigation Water: Owner Guide 2026, How to Turn Meter Valve ON/OFF

fact: Poudre Tech Metropolitan District diverts its irrigation water from the Cache la Poudre River through the Eaton and Whitney ditches, stores it in seven irrigation lakes, and filters it through 300-micron filters before pumping it to each yard's non-potable meter.
quote: Getting the water: We divert raw water from the Cache la Poudre River through the Eaton and Whitney Ditches. • Storing it: The water is stored in one of the District's seven irrigation lakes. … • Filtering: Before it reaches your property, the water is filtered through 300-micron filters at our pump stations. • Delivering it: The water is pumped through pressure zones and a connected pipeline system that carries it directly to the non-potable meter in your yard.
source_label: RainDance and Poudre Tech Metropolitan District, Water Rate Fact Sheet 2026

fact: The Water Valley Company says the first home in Water Valley was built in 1995 and the community now has more than 2,500 residential units, a 27-hole golf course, miles of trails, sandy beaches and five man-made lakes.
quote: The first home in the Water Valley master-planned community was constructed in Windsor. Today, Water Valley features more than 2,500 residential units, a 27-hole golf course, miles of trails, sandy beaches, five man-made lakes, tennis and pickle ball courts, and commercial and retail businesses.
source_label: The Water Valley Company, Our Story (timeline entry 1995; watervalley.com/our-story/ redirects here)

fact: Pelican Lakes Golf Course in Water Valley, designed by Ted Robinson Sr. and opened July 12, 1999, plays 7,264 yards among more than 300 surface acres of water, with four man-made lakes in play on 10 holes, and its club says no homes sit directly on the course.
quote: WINDSOR'S PELICAN LAKES GOLF COURSE AND SEMI-PRIVATE COUNTRY CLUB … There are over 300 surface acres of water at Pelican Lakes, most of it stemming from the Cache la Poudre River that snakes its way through the entire 7,264-yard course. Four man-made lakes surround the remaining perimeter of Pelican Lakes and come into play on 10 of the holes. … The facility is also in the middle of a housing development, yet none of the new homes in Windsor, CO are directly on the golf course. … Designed by Ted Robinson Sr. Opened July 12th, 1999
source_label: Pelican Lakes Resort & Golf, Pelican Lakes Course page

fact: Pelican Lakes' club describes its nine-hole Pelican Falls course as the one with homes beside the fairways.
quote: If your dream is to live on a fairway, The Falls golf course has beautiful homes just a chip shot away.
source_label: Pelican Lakes Resort & Golf, Pelican Falls Course page

fact: Trumark Homes described Pelican Shores in 2022 as a lakefront neighborhood in Water Valley with 51 interior lots and eight waterfront lots, whose HOA dues include landscape maintenance and non-potable water.
quote: Pelican Shores has six gorgeous floor plans on 51 interior lots. … There are eight amazing waterfront lots with four distinctive plans to choose from. … include these services: landscape maintenance, snow removal, trash removal, and non-potable water.
source_label: Trumark Homes blog, Trumark Homes Takes Colorado: 10 Things You Need To Know About Pelican Shores (February 10, 2022)
notes: A builder's sales post, not an HOA document; the page uses it only to send Pelican Shores owners to their own association first.
